match_note: The rebuttal's 'Old' text matches v1: v1 says the nuclear spin can be driven 'irrespective of its hybridization', attributes the high-field signal drop to the RF amplitude as 'the dominant factor', and proposes piezoelectric displacement driving; the revised wording, setpoint study and rate-equation model are absent from v1.

concerns.quote: While the selection-rule argument suggests that an oscillating B field drives the NMR transition, it does not tell more than that.
concerns.summary: The proposed driving mechanism (effective oscillating magnetic field via piezoelectric motion or tip dipolar field) is not substantiated, is implausibly weak, and alternatives are not rigorously excluded.

concerns.quote: Quantitative estimates of the resulting B1 fields and comparison to the observations.
concerns.summary: No quantitative estimate of the driving field B1 is compared with the data.

concerns.quote: the modulation of the hyperfine interaction (A) is dismissed quite quickly.
concerns.summary: Hyperfine modulation as a driving mechanism is dismissed too quickly and should be discussed further.

concerns.quote: Have the authors tried to measure NMR at different tip fields?
concerns.summary: Measurements at different tips or tip-atom distances (tip fields) are needed to test the driving mechanism.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is unclear why the static tip field does not affect the nuclear Zeeman energy (Eq. 1).
concerns.summary: The tip field's contribution to the nuclear Zeeman term is omitted from the Hamiltonian without justification, inconsistent with tip-field driving.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The absence of Δml = ±2 transitions is used as an argument, but this could also be due to sensitivity limits.
concerns.summary: Ruling out quadrupole modulation from the absence of Δm=±2 transitions may reflect sensitivity limits.

concerns.quote: With their data, I believe the authors can well capture the nuclear relaxation channels and rates involved in this system via simulations of spin dynamics.
concerns.summary: Spin-dynamics simulations could extract nuclear relaxation channels and rates, a key use of CW-ENDOR.

concerns.quote: The interpretation of ESR peak heights as time-averaged nuclear spin populations is standard but deserves more discussion.
concerns.summary: Reading ESR peak heights as nuclear populations needs a rate-equation model including spin pumping, relaxation and ESR driving.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: I recommend to clarify whether the key advance is methodological (ENDOR) or material-specific (properties of Ti at the oxygen binding site of MgO) in comparison to the previous work
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the advance over earlier Cu ENDOR work is the method or the weaker hybridization of Ti.

concerns.quote: I think it is difficult to conclude that the driving is independent from the hybridization.
concerns.summary: The central claim of driving independent of hybridization is not shown; residual hybridization should be quantified and NMR intensity versus VNMR checked, or the wording moderated.

concerns.quote: The manuscript does not demonstrate manipulation of the local environment to influence nuclear spin properties.
concerns.summary: The introduction stresses STM control of the local environment, which is not exercised in this work.

concerns.quote: the authors cite Ref. 34 in support of hybridization reducing nuclear spin lifetime. Does this paper show the hybridization-dependent lifetime?
concerns.summary: A cited reference does not show what it is cited for (hybridization-dependent nuclear lifetime).

concerns.quote: Why did the authors modulate ESR not NMR? By modulating ESR signals at different peaks (different frequencies), the background would be significantly different
concerns.summary: The choice to modulate the ESR rather than the NMR drive affects backgrounds and needs justification.

concerns.quote: In Fig. 2a, the red curve shows peaks instead of dips, while Fig. 2b shows dips for all transitions.
concerns.summary: Figs. 2a and 2b appear inconsistent in sign and in which transitions appear at the second ESR peak.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: in Fig. 2b, only five peaks are given although 6 ESR transitions exist.
concerns.summary: Fig. 2b shows only five of six ESR peaks without explanation.

concerns.quote: All peaks appear comparable to the noise level. Extracting four peaks from this set of data may introduce significant uncertainty
concerns.summary: Fitting four NMR peaks in Fig. 3a is unreliable because the features are at the noise level; why III and IV should appear is also unclear.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The manuscript attributes the decrease in signal at high magnetic fields primarily to RF transmission limitations. This is plausible but not fully disentangled from intrinsic physics.
concerns.summary: The high-field signal loss may be intrinsic rather than due to RF transmission; signals should be compared at fixed lowest RF power.

concerns.quote: The manuscript would benefit from a brief explanation of how the RF power used for the nuclear drive compares to that used in ESR measurements
concerns.summary: Compare the RF power for nuclear and electron driving and what it implies for driving rates.

concerns.quote: It would be helpful to include a brief discussion of the relevant energy scales of the electronic and nuclear Zeeman terms
concerns.summary: State the energy scales of electron and nuclear Zeeman terms for this experiment.

concerns.quote: The discussion concerning the determination of the sign of the hyperfine (A) and quadrupolar (Q) parameters is somewhat difficult to follow.
concerns.summary: The determination of the signs of A and Q is hard to follow.

concerns.quote: Lock-in cycle B. Please try to include those in the figures
concerns.summary: Lock-in cycle B should be shown to explain the lineshapes in Fig. 2a.

concerns.quote: It can be difficult to distinguish the two colors in Fig. 1e, especially after printing.
concerns.summary: Fig. 1e colors and their relation to experimental conditions are unclear.

concerns.quote: Fig. 3 main caption doesn’t read. Fig. 2a could benefit from clearer labeling of the corresponding (m_I) states.
concerns.summary: Fig. 3 caption is ungrammatical and Fig. 2a lacks m_I labels.

concerns.quote: Figure 1c is rather schematic and lacks quantitative scale.
concerns.summary: Fig. 1c needs quantitative scales.

concerns.quote: Frequent missing articles
concerns.summary: Grammar, ambiguous pronouns and inconsistent italic notation throughout main text and SI.

later_concerns.quote: I remain somewhat skeptical as to whether the polarization mechanisms for Cu and Ti can be considered the same.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: explain how the ~80 mV excitation polarizes the Ti nuclear spin and whether polarization depends on hybridization.

later_concerns.quote: I also recommend making the color convention consistent between the panels.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: color conventions and signs of features differ between Figs. 2a and 2b.

later_concerns.quote: RFig. 2 and Fig. 2a seem to indicate that the NMR transitions occur at approximately the same frequencies (~45 MHz and ~80 MHz), whereas Fig. 2b appears to show different transition frequencies.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: apparent discrepancy in NMR transition frequencies between figures, and unclear expected sign of each transition.

later_concerns.quote: How exactly is the background defined?
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: the background subtraction in the 2D map is undefined and shifts off-resonance signal below zero.

later_concerns.quote: Could the authors indicate more clearly where these four transitions are observed, for example by marking them explicitly in the figure?
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: the four inner transitions in Fig. 2b are not identifiable; mark them.
